text.arabic_uthmani: لَهُم مَّا يَشَآءُونَ فِيهَا وَلَدَيْنَا مَزِيدٌۭ

words.gloss_range: fronted lām of benefit, possession, and entitlement in a nominal predicate; purpose and motion-direction senses are not selected here
words.prose: {{ar:لَ}} ({{tr:la}}) opens the ayah by assigning the promise to its recipients before the wished content is named. Its force is not a motion-direction or purpose clause; it is the compact governor that turns the following pronoun into the fronted predicate of entitlement. The result is recipient-first architecture: the reader first hears that the promised domain is for them, and only afterward hears how wide that domain becomes. The nasal close of hum runs straight into mā, so even the sound binds the recipient frame to the open relative content.

topics.headline: fronted entitlement predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that entitlement is the first grammatical fact of the ayah, before any desired content is specified.
topics.reason: The local syntax makes the lām-pronoun complex the fronted predicate for the delayed relative subject, so benefit and possession survive while purpose and motion-direction are outside the local construction.

topics.headline: bound prepositional completion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees entitlement as a bound grammatical relation, not as a free-standing label attached after the fact.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify the word as a governing preposition whose force is completed by the following governed pronoun.

topics.headline: recipient-first architecture
topics.reader_payoff: The reader parses the first beat through the recipients before parsing the open set of what they will.
topics.reason: The predicate precedes the delayed subject, making the recipient frame structurally prior to the relative content.

topics.headline: recipient-to-relative sound link
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the opening beneficiary frame bind immediately into the open relative phrase.
topics.reason: The first audible unit begins the entitlement frame, and the following nasal-to-relative contact supports the row's sound-level observation.

words.gloss_range: third-person masculine plural pronoun governed by the preceding lām, marking the tracked group as recipients rather than the clause subject
words.prose: {{ar:هُمْ}} ({{tr:hum}}) does two jobs at once. Because it is governed after the lām, it keeps the recipients inside the fronted predicate rather than making them the subject of the clause. Because it is a definite third-person plural pronoun, it also resumes the already tracked righteous entrants and turns the commanded addressees from the prior scene into narrated possessors of what they will.

topics.headline: governed recipient pronoun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the pronoun is recipient-predicate material, not the subject that carries the clause.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence governs the pronoun through the lām and identifies the complex as the fronted predicate.

topics.headline: recoverable plural recipients
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the reward assigned to a recoverable plural group, not introduced as a new unnamed class.
topics.reason: Cross-reference evidence links the pronoun to the plural group carried by the preceding promise and command.

topics.headline: beneficiary becomes willing subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks one group moving from commanded entrants to beneficiaries and then to agents of willing.
topics.reason: The same plural group is marked here as beneficiary and later carried by the verb's 3mp agreement.

words.gloss_range: headless relative pronoun functioning as the delayed subject and object-domain of the relative verb; negative and interrogative parses are blocked locally
words.prose: {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) is the open content-word of the first beat. Grammatically it is anchored enough to serve as the delayed subject of the nominal clause, yet semantically it leaves the referent unrestricted: whatever falls under their willing. The following verb and locative tail stay inside its relative scope, so the first beat is not a vague abundance claim but a complete entitlement frame whose object-domain, action, and place belong together. Its long-vowel cadence stretches that open relative phrase across the beat under the recipient frame.

topics.headline: open relative as delayed subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the open set itself is what is for them, rather than a named class of blessings.
topics.reason: QAC marks a relative pronoun, and local syntax makes the relative phrase the delayed subject of the fronted predicate.

topics.headline: verb and locative inside scope
topics.reader_payoff: The reader keeps the willing verb and paradise domain inside the same relative content slot.
topics.reason: The relative clause runs through the verb and locative phrase, with the relative pronoun also supplying the verb's object.

topics.headline: mobile particle locally fixed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees a highly mobile particle locally converted into an unrestricted relative object-domain.
topics.reason: The surface can serve other functions elsewhere, but the local nominal sentence and following imperfect verb force the relative parse here.

topics.headline: assigned openness in sound and order
topics.reader_payoff: The reader both parses and hears the open category as stretched across the first beat under the recipient frame.
topics.reason: Fronting assigns the relative subject to the recipients, while the long-vowel cadence supports the row's sound-level observation.

words.gloss_range: imperfect 3mp finite verb of willing, wishing, desiring, or choosing inside the relative clause, with its object supplied by the preceding relative pronoun
words.root_gloss_range: willing and thingness are relevant as root-family pressure, but the local finite verb selects active human willing rather than an abstract decree noun or an ontological claim
words.prose: {{ar:يَشَآءُونَ}} ({{tr:yashāʾūna}}) makes the open content renewable rather than closed. Its 3mp imperfect form carries the same plural group inside the verb, so the recipients are not only beneficiaries but ongoing agents of willing. The root {{ar:ش ي أ}} ({{tr:sh-y-ʾ}}) lets wish, will, desire, and choosing remain live, while the local grammar narrows the claim: the verb specifies the relative object-domain; it does not turn human desire into an independent creation act. The word uses a common Quranic imperfect channel, but here that ordinary channel becomes the center of a familiar paradise formula also seen in 16:31, 25:16, 39:34, and 42:22. Its hamza catches inside the long-vowel first beat after the secured entry scene, and in this ayah's sequence fulfilled willing is then surpassed by the final surplus, contrasting with the more-demand of 50:30 and carrying forward the promise of 50:32.

topics.headline: verb defines the relative object-domain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the verb specifying the open relative content rather than launching a separate event clause.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the relative pronoun the explicit object of the verb and keeps the verb inside the relative clause.

topics.headline: ongoing plural willing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices continuing group agency carried by the verb form, not a single completed request.
topics.reason: The imperfect 3mp form and implicit-subject evidence identify ongoing plural agency tied to the same promised group.

topics.headline: wish, will, and thingness pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears active choosing and willing, not merely passive appetite, while keeping the claim within the finite verb's grammar.
topics.reason: The root-family claim survives as semantic pressure, but missing V4 rows and the local finite verb prevent overreading it as independent ontological production.

topics.headline: finite imperfect instead of other root channels
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ayah choose enacted ongoing willing rather than a causative frame, completed perfect, or abstract volition noun.
topics.reason: The local QAC form is imperfect active 3mp; broader root alternatives can contrast with that selection but do not replace it.

topics.headline: common imperfect channel
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the word is powerful here through ordinary Quranic imperfect usage, not through rarity.
topics.reason: Contextual evidence shows this root/form channel is common and heavily imperfect, supporting salience by placement rather than rare form.

topics.headline: paradise formula exceeded by surplus
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes a familiar paradise formula that 50:35 locally expands by adding surplus beyond fulfilled willing.
topics.reason: The rows cite the recurring paradise formula and the local sequence from willing to surplus; the concrete cross-surah formula references include 16:31, 25:16, 39:34, and 42:22.

topics.headline: same-surah contrast and promise thread
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees paradise desire satisfied before surplus appears, in contrast with the earlier demand for more in 50:30 and in continuity with the promise in 50:32.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows provide concrete same-surah links to 50:30 and 50:32; they illuminate contrast and promise-fulfillment without changing the local parse.

topics.headline: audible will inside first beat
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the will-verb as the center of a long-vowel first beat that follows the secured entry scene.
topics.reason: The sound rows concern the hamza and vowel chain, and the boundary row links the verb's exercised willing to the prior entry in peace.

topics.headline: human willing as threshold
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees human willing complete the first beat and become the threshold that the divine surplus surpasses.
topics.reason: The relative construction completes before the conjunction, and the verb's placement after the relative head defines the open subject before the surplus clause begins.

words.gloss_range: locative preposition plus feminine singular suffix, locating the wished content within the recovered paradise domain
words.prose: {{ar:فِيهَا}} ({{tr:fīhā}}) closes the first beat by giving desire its place. The fused preposition and feminine suffix retrieve paradise from the prior discourse without renaming it, so the wished content is not abstractly available but located within that domain. The word also prepares the contrast with the next clause: desire operates inside paradise, while the surplus is held in divine presence rather than merely circulating inside the same interior.

topics.headline: paradise domain recovered by suffix
topics.reader_payoff: The reader identifies the location of fulfilled willing as the recovered paradise domain, not an unnamed abstraction.
topics.reason: Cross-reference evidence resolves the feminine suffix to the garden introduced in 50:31.

topics.headline: locative boundary of the first beat
topics.reader_payoff: The reader keeps the place phrase as the operating domain for wishing and wished things.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence ties the prepositional phrase to the relative verb and makes it the location of the willing frame.

topics.headline: inside paradise versus with Us
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the contrast between the interior where desire operates and the divine-presence frame where surplus is kept.
topics.reason: The first locative phrase closes the desire beat, and the following presence phrase begins the surplus beat.

topics.headline: compact continuity across boundary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees one paradise referent continue from entry to the domain of desire through a compact suffix rather than repetition.
topics.reason: The suffix is feminine singular and anaphoric, preserving the prior paradise referent while shifting its role to locative domain.

topics.headline: delayed locative close
topics.reader_payoff: The reader first hears desire as open, then hears the final word of the beat supply its domain.
topics.reason: The prepositional phrase follows the verb and closes the relative phrase before the conjunction.

words.gloss_range: clitic conjunction and clause hinge, joining the fulfilled-wish beat to a distinct divine-surplus declaration while allowing additive, resumptive, and circumstantial force
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) is the hinge that keeps the two beats together without flattening them into one list. It can coordinate, resume, or carry a circumstantial contrast: they have what they will, and more remains with Us. Because the particle is so minimal and clitic, the turn into the divine-presence phrase is immediate; the fulfilled-wish clause is complete, yet the next clause is attached as surplus rather than replacement.

topics.headline: additive, resumptive, and circumstantial hinge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the surplus is both connected to fulfilled desire and protected from becoming just another wished item.
topics.reason: The conjunction coordinates the second nominal clause after the first, while the CRITICAL rows preserve valid additive, resumptive, and circumstantial readings.

topics.headline: contrast keeps surplus beyond wish-list
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the conjunction making excess meaningful after full wish-fulfillment, not undoing or replacing that fulfillment.
topics.reason: The two-beat structure lets coordination and contrast both survive because the second clause follows a completed wish-fulfillment clause.

topics.headline: minimal clitic pivot
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the turn into divine reserve arrive sharply, with almost no lexical weight before the next predicate.
topics.reason: The one-letter conjunction is prefixed in recitation to the following phrase, making the structural pivot immediate.

topics.headline: axis from human will to divine reserve
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the ayah turn from what is for them to what is with Us at the exact conjunction.
topics.reason: The conjunction sits between two complete nominal structures and marks the shift from third-person recipients to first-person divine possession.

topics.headline: connected but protected surplus
topics.reader_payoff: The reader keeps the surplus related to the fulfilled wish while still recognizing it as beyond that clause.
topics.reason: The ambiguity is meaningful only because the first clause is complete and the second clause introduces a new reserve frame.

words.gloss_range: fronted adverbial predicate of immediate divine presence, possession, and keeping, with first-person plural suffix bound into the place-word
words.prose: {{ar:لَدَيْنَا}} ({{tr:ladaynā}}) opens the second beat by relocating value from the recipients' domain to immediate divine keeping. The word is not a loose setting phrase; it is the fronted predicate before the delayed surplus noun. Its first-person plural suffix turns the scene from third-person recipients into direct divine self-reference, and its fixed adverbial presence makes the surplus held with Us rather than simply inside paradise.

topics.headline: immediate divine keeping
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the surplus is located in immediate divine custody, not merely added inside the recipients' domain.
topics.reason: The word is an adverbial predicate of proximity and possession before the delayed subject, supporting presence and keeping together.

topics.headline: third-person recipients to first-person speaker
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the surplus enter as direct divine self-disclosure after a third-person recipient clause.
topics.reason: The suffix marks first-person plural divine possession and shifts the speaker-axis after the third-person plural forms.

topics.headline: fronted reserve predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader learns where the surplus is held before the surplus noun itself arrives.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes this word the fronted predicate for the delayed subject of the second nominal clause.

topics.headline: source beyond paradise interior
topics.reader_payoff: The reader distinguishes the interior domain of fulfilled desire from a reserve whose source is with the divine speaker.
topics.reason: The second beat moves to a divine reserve frame after the first beat's paradise domain.

topics.headline: fixed adverbial form fused with speaker
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees place and speaker compressed into one predicate rather than a productive root competing with nearby roots.
topics.reason: The evidence treats the word as a fixed adverbial presence form with a bound first-person plural suffix.

topics.headline: mirrored predicate and cadence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader compares the first beat's recipient predicate with the second beat's divine-presence predicate.
topics.reason: The second predicate mirrors the first predicate-first slot while sound and boundary rows reinforce the comparison.

topics.headline: pronoun, position, and proximity converge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees person shift, predicate fronting, and proximity combine into a single divine-reserve frame.
topics.reason: The convergent row accurately summarizes locally supported grammar, pronoun reference, and proximity semantics.

words.gloss_range: indefinite nominative mīm-maṣdar noun meaning added increase or surplus, locally the delayed subject held with the divine speaker after fulfilled desire
words.root_gloss_range: increase, augmentation, surplus, and provision/reserve are relevant; local grammar selects a held surplus beyond completion, not self-increase, overdoing, bidding for more, or a specified item
words.prose: {{ar:مَزِيدٌ}} ({{tr:mazīdun}}) is the final open noun of the ayah. Its nominative case makes it the delayed subject of the second nominal clause, not another object wished for, and its singular indefiniteness gathers surplus into one unitemized, audible open ending. The root {{ar:ز ي د}} ({{tr:z-y-d}}) brings increase, addedness, and provision-like reserve into the word, while the local frame narrows that field to excess held with the divine speaker after desire has already been fulfilled, not self-increase or embellishing overstatement. The same rare mīm-form stands where increase exceeds willing and answers the earlier more-question in 50:30 by changing case and scene: here the more is not an insatiable demand but a granted reserve. Classical reception can hear the vision horizon of 10:26, but the local indefinite does not name only that referent. Across the boundary from 50:34, unquantified peace at entry opens into unquantified surplus at closure, so the entered paradise scene resolves by opening beyond itself with the divine speaker.

topics.headline: unqualified final surplus
topics.reader_payoff: The reader ends on an unspecified surplus whose kind and limit are withheld rather than itemized.
topics.reason: The noun is nominative indefinite, clause-final, and lacks adjective, genitive complement, or explanatory clause.

topics.headline: delayed subject not wished object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader protects the surplus from being absorbed into the earlier wish-object category.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence parses the preceding presence phrase as fronted predicate and this nominative noun as the delayed subject.

topics.headline: mīm noun presents held addedness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees increase presented as a held noun-like surplus, not only as an action being performed.
topics.reason: The form tag identifies a mīm maṣdar noun; the process/product description survives, while same-form V4 examples are absent and therefore do not expand the local claim.

topics.headline: increase beyond fulfilled desire
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the more as excess after completion, not compensation for lack.
topics.reason: The root's increase field is locally sequenced after the first beat has already granted whatever they will.

topics.headline: provision-like supplied reserve
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can feel the surplus as supplied reserve beyond request, while leaving its quantity, quality, duration, and rank open.
topics.reason: V4 includes a provision branch and broader increase dimensions; the local noun permits reserve-color but does not specify a concrete provision item.

topics.headline: nonlocal increase branches excluded
topics.reader_payoff: The reader keeps divine held surplus distinct from self-increase, embellishing intensification, or other nonlocal increase branches.
topics.reason: The selected mīm noun in the divine-reserve clause contrasts with reflexive, Form II, and overdoing branches without activating them locally.

topics.headline: one open noun gathers surplus
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears one capacious open term rather than a list of separate additions or a numerical claim.
topics.reason: The noun is singular, indefinite, and unmodified, allowing scope-intensification without itemization.

topics.headline: audible indefinite close
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the ayah close on an open indefinite sound rather than on a specified complement.
topics.reason: The final tanwīn is both grammatical indefiniteness and the recited ending of the ayah.

topics.headline: rare form paired with willing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees a narrow mīm-form selected at the point where increase exceeds willing.
topics.reason: Contextual evidence marks the exact root/form as low-occurrence, and the local order pairs it after the willing verb.

topics.headline: 50:30 more-question answered in reward close
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the rare more-word move from the punishment question in 50:30 to a granted surplus in 50:35.
topics.reason: The rows give a concrete same-surah echo at 50:30 and contrast its demand/question scene with this divine-reserve assertion.

topics.headline: same form with changed case and scene
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that near-identical sound is redirected by case and scene from demand to promised reserve.
topics.reason: The echo rows specify 50:30 and the local nominative subject role; contextual evidence supports the form's rarity.

topics.headline: classical vision association as horizon
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notes a classical reception horizon linking the more to vision in 10:26 without forcing the local indefinite noun to name only that referent.
topics.reason: The row cites 10:26 and a classical interpretive link, but the local noun remains indefinite and unqualified.

topics.headline: general surplus tail after wish fulfillment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ayah framed from recipient entitlement to final surplus beyond them with Us.
topics.reason: The second nominal tail follows the specific wish-fulfillment clause and closes the ayah with a nonformulaic surplus pairing.

topics.headline: unbounded peace to unbounded surplus
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the boundary move from unquantified peace at entry to unquantified excess at the close.
topics.reason: The boundary rows link the indefinite entry noun from 50:34 with the indefinite surplus noun at 50:35.

topics.headline: entered domain opens beyond itself
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the entered paradise scene resolve not by stopping inside the domain but by opening onto continuing surplus with the divine speaker.
topics.reason: The boundary and convergent rows combine final position, rare form, and same-surah echo to make the surplus the closing scene marker.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: مَا يَشَاءُونَ فِيهَا: an unrestricted object is governed by their wishing and located within the garden.
baseline_models.mechanism: The thing branch makes the object determinate, while the volition branch makes it an object of will; لَهُم assigns the resulting availability to them.

activation_trace.role: The knowable, reportable thing image lets مَا يَشَاءُونَ range over anything that can become a determinate object of enjoyment.
Will directed toward a thing supplies the clause's volitional engine and centers recipient agency.

changed_reading.after: Within it, whatever becomes an object of their will is available to them; the clause foregrounds their agency, not a fixed menu.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: وَلَدَيْنَا مَزِيدٌ follows the already exhaustive مَا يَشَاءُونَ.
baseline_models.mechanism: The switch from لَهُم to لَدَيْنَا places increase at a source beyond the recipients' own horizon of wishing.

activation_trace.role: Increase and growth make مَزِيدٌ an open surplus beyond wish-fulfillment rather than one additional listed object.

changed_reading.before: An extra reward is added to the promised goods.
changed_reading.after: Even after unrestricted wish-fulfillment, independently sourced increase remains with God, leaving abundance structurally open-ended.

context_deltas.mechanism: Earthly loss is paired with preservation 'with Us,' then blessed descent produces gardens, provision, and life; مَزِيدٌ becomes the far end of a loss-preservation-regrowth arc.

activation_trace.role: Increase and growth name the culminating surplus generated after recovery.
The going-away of part of a thing supplies the initial material deficit that surplus reverses.
Guarding and preserving prevent earthly diminution from becoming final loss.
Caused growth from planting supplies a visible mechanism by which a source turns descent into abundance.
Apportioned giving identifies the generated abundance as provision for recipients.
Earth revived by rain and growth turns replacement into renewed generativity, not bare restitution.

structural_cues: 50:4's وَعِندَنَا answers diminution with preservation; 50:9-11 then stages descent, growth, provision, and revival before 50:35's وَلَدَيْنَا مَزِيدٌ.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies deficit, divine preservation, and a growth-to-life sequence; I infer a causal arc from preserved loss to surplus. A live alternative is that these scenes prove resurrection only, without defining paradisal increase.

changed_reading.before: The 'more' is an arbitrary bonus after restoration.
changed_reading.after: The 'more' crowns a demonstrated divine pattern: loss is preserved, restored, and then made generative beyond its former measure.

context_deltas.mechanism: Knowledge of hidden self-talk joined to extreme nearness recasts wishing as inward attraction already legible at its source, not merely an articulated request.

activation_trace.role: The soul's attraction to a thing supplies a pre-verbal layer of يَشَاءُونَ beneath explicit choosing.
Hidden self-talk makes inward motion available to divine knowledge before it becomes speech.
Nearness turns لَدَيْنَا from remote storage into proximity to the source that knows desire.

structural_cues: 50:16 coordinates 'We know' and 'We are nearer'; 50:35 coordinates their wishing and 'with Us.'
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies hidden inward speech and divine nearness; I carry that relational pattern into the focus clause and treat attraction as recognizable before petition. Alternatively, 50:16 may concern surveillance and judgment rather than responsive generosity.

changed_reading.before: They receive whatever wishes they can formulate.
changed_reading.after: Their inward attractions are already known at the near divine source, so fulfillment need not wait on a spoken inventory of wants.

context_deltas.mechanism: A filled vessel asks whether there is more in 50:30; five ayat later God declares that more is with Him after every wish is met. The repeated noun splits insatiable intake from sourced gift.

activation_trace.role: Fullness equal to a container defines Hell's capacity frame, within which its demand for more remains unclosed.
Increase appears as a question from the consuming side, supplying the negative pole of the contrast.
The same increase is now declaratively located with the giver after recipients already possess what they wish.

structural_cues: هَلْ مِن مَّزِيدٍ in 50:30 and وَلَدَيْنَا مَزِيدٌ in 50:35 bracket the garden's nearness, promise, entry, and permanence.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies exact lexical recurrence, container-fullness, and opposed destinations; I infer an antithetical hinge between consuming demand and giving surplus. A live alternative is simple repetition of unbounded continuation without moral contrast.

changed_reading.before: Both occurrences of مَزِيدٌ merely mean another quantity.
changed_reading.after: The focus 'more' is defined against appetite that asks to be fed: it is surplus proceeding from a giver after desire is fulfilled, not lack perpetuating consumption.

context_deltas.mechanism: The garden is brought near, entered in safety, and named a day of abiding before wish and surplus are announced; increase therefore operates after arrival rather than merely purchasing admission.

activation_trace.role: Movement into nearness presents the destination to its recipients before the focus surplus appears.
Entry into the interior marks admission as already complete, so مَزِيدٌ cannot be merely access.
Safety from harm removes repair and threat-management as the sole content of subsequent wishing.
Abiding resistant to decay gives the ensuing increase an open temporal field.
Growth after secure entry functions as continuing hospitality rather than an admission grant.

structural_cues: The uninterrupted 50:31-35 sequence moves from approach to entry to abiding, then to wishing and divine surplus.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies completed entry, safety, permanence, and then increase; I infer that permanence gives growth room to continue after arrival. Alternatively, permanence may qualify residence while مَزِيدٌ remains a single added gift.

changed_reading.before: The reward is a package delivered upon admission.
changed_reading.after: Admission and safety are already complete; the 'more' names continuing hospitality within an abiding life, not the price or content of entry.

context_deltas.mechanism: Creation without fatigue makes divine increase a sign of undiminished productive capacity, not leftovers from a finite store.

activation_trace.role: Growth names the positive output whose source remains undiminished.
Negated weakness and fatigue remove depletion from the model of divine production.

structural_cues: The no-fatigue creation statement follows the focus promise by three ayat and reopens the surah's earlier creation evidence.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a categorical denial of fatigue in creation; I extend non-depletion from creating worlds to granting surplus. The narrower alternative confines the denial to the six-day creation claim.

changed_reading.before: The 'more' is a large but potentially countable reserve.
changed_reading.after: The 'more' points to a source whose giving does not consume its productive capacity, so abundance is not rationed by exertion.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus inventory permits a coercive carry-to-an-affair branch for ش ي ء, but the surah's closing negation of compulsion suppresses that branch and sharpens يَشَاءُونَ as owned volition.

activation_trace.role: Being carried or compelled into an affair exposes a coercive possibility that the context can explicitly reject.
Will directed toward a thing remains as the positive branch once coercion is screened out.
Coercive domination is explicitly negated, functioning as a contextual brake on reading wish-fulfillment as imposed desire.

structural_cues: The closing address negates coercion and replaces it with reminder; the focus assigns the paradisal object to what recipients themselves will.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a coercive branch and an explicit anti-compulsion close; I extend that discourse posture to the agency marked in يَشَاءُونَ. The live alternative limits 50:45 to prophetic method and gives it no paradisal force.

changed_reading.before: Perfect reward could mean recipients are made to want what is assigned.
changed_reading.after: The clause preserves owned willing: goods answer their agency, while divine 'more' exceeds that agency as gift rather than coercively rewriting it.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because the occurrence is ز ي د while the activated split target is ز و د. It remains packet-licensed and anchored to مَزِيدٌ through the supplied mapped inventory, but downstream prose should call it a form-distant echo of provision, not a lexical gloss or settled interpretation.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The split mapping for focus-word مَزِيدٌ includes ز و د, whose first branch is provision carried for transition.

activation_trace.role: Carried provision for movement recasts divine 'more' as supply for onward life beyond each attained satisfaction.

changed_reading.before: مَزِيدٌ only adds quantity at a final, static destination.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the divine surplus also sounds like provision for continued movement within an unending destination.

strongest_changes: The same مَزِيدٌ that voices Hell's demand becomes, in the focus, giver-sourced surplus after every wish is fulfilled.
Earlier diminution, preservation, growth, provision, and revival turn 'more' from an arbitrary bonus into the climax of a restorative-generative pattern.
Because approach, entry, safety, and abiding precede 50:35, the surplus reads as continuing post-entry hospitality.
summary.what_was_special: The focus balances exhaustive recipient agency with a remainder located at the divine source; context makes that remainder simultaneously anti-deficit, anti-consumption, post-arrival, and non-depleting without collapsing those mechanisms into one gloss.
remaining_uncertainties: The hidden-desire model depends on carrying 50:16's nearness from judicial knowledge into beneficent responsiveness.
The no-fatigue model transfers a creation claim to ongoing giving.
The anti-coercion and ز و د provision readings are live but deliberately exploratory because their branch and discourse transfers are more distant.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Human willing is contained within an unexhausted divine surplus.** The willing variant of `ش ي ء:B001` supplies desire, `ز ي د:B001` increase, and `ز ي د:B002` surplus. The two locatives distinguish “in it” from “with Us.” I infer a nested provision model: fulfilled creaturely willing does not exhaust the giver's capacity. The ayah reads as satisfaction plus open-ended excess.
2. **The same `مَزِيد` reverses 50:30.** `ز ي د:B004` supplies seeking more there, while here `ز ي د:B002` is surplus held with the giver. The packet supplies lexical repetition across opposite destinations; I infer a moral reversal between insatiable intake and bestowed abundance. The word retains two distinct mechanisms rather than one blended sense.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 50:38's creation without exhaustion supplied a later causal ground for unexhausted surplus. The abundance of 50:35 reads not as a finite stock but as provision from agency untouched by productive weariness.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Effective will is distinguished from appetite for increase.** The willing variant of `ش ي ء B002` supplies will directed toward a thing, with the source note that attaining it may be implied; `ز ي د B001` supplies bestowed increase. Five ayat earlier, a full Hell asks for more under `ز ي د B004`; here possession (*lahum*) precedes the additional gift (*ladaynā*). The packet supplies that lexical mirror; I infer that fulfilled will has a settled object while surplus comes from the giver. “More” reads as abundance beyond sufficiency, not appetite unable to register fullness.

2. **Will carries a dormant listening-history.** The listening-closely variant of `ش ي ء B006` is activated by 50:37’s deliberate casting of hearing and by the ordered praise of 50:39–40. The fixed morphology remains willing, but the packet places future desire beside prior receptive attention and disciplined response. I infer that the will expressed in the garden is not arbitrary impulse: it is the matured counterpart of a self that learned to listen. This is exploratory because the accepted listening image is a variant resonance, not the direct verbal construction in *yashāʾūn*.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 50:37 supplied the surprising activation of the listening variant in `ش ي ء B006`: the one who casts hearing provides a receptive history for later willing. 50:39–40’s disciplined praise strengthened that correction by showing desire emerging from practiced orientation rather than raw appetite.

concept_map.definition: İleride, özellikle yolculukta kullanılmak üzere o anki gereksinimin ötesinde yiyecek veya su ayırmak ve yanına almaktır. Bu dal, ayrılan yiyecek ile suyu taşımaya yarayan deri torba ve su kaplarını da kapsar.

facets.statement: Yiyecek veya su, o anki gereksinimin ötesinde ileride ve özellikle yolculukta kullanılmak üzere saklanır.
Bu saklanmış yiyecek ya da suyu edinmek ve yol için yanına almak hazırlık eylemini oluşturur.
Yol yiyeceğinin konduğu deri torba ile suyun konduğu taşıma kabı, hazırlanan gerecin kaplarına verilen adlardır.

facets.statement: Bir yolculuk veya başka bir geçiş için gerekecek yiyecek ve araçları önceden hazırlamak ya da edinmek.

İşi, kazancı, iyi veya kötü davranışı kişinin bir geçişte yanında taşıdığı birikim gibi değerlendirmek.
Başka birine yol veya geçiş sırasında kullanacağı yiyecek ve gereçleri vermek.
